description:
## Goal

Make Ty identity denotational at Types::intern. Within the supported type domain, mutually-subtype immutable types intern to one Ty, independent of construction and publication order.

## Authority

Types::intern is the only normalization authority. World memoizes typed comparisons by operation and interned operands. Callable code identity, callable surface constraints, captures and runtime observation remain distinct typed concepts.

Do not normalize with canonical rendering, raw Ty order, a local activation normalizer, an arena sweep or a second equivalence authority. This ticket does not claim that the current structural type language can represent recursive denotations; fz-kdt.177 owns that missing representation.

## TDD

Prove every currently supported equivalent construction order returns the same Ty identity, including empty-list versus list unions, equivalent tuple carvings, template and ground forms, and anonymous versus branded callable controls. Equal reproduction wakes nobody. Cross-process type, activation, executable, product and artifact identities are deterministic.

Audit sorts whose only purpose is keep-first or raw interner-order sensitivity. Retain presentation order only where it is actually observable.

## Deletion and acceptance

Delete duplicate equivalence normalization, order-sensitive survivor selection and compensating sort logic. Record bounded comparison and interning work. Full focused, corpus, three-door, deterministic, documentation, formatting, check and strict-Clippy gates pass; fresh ticket-scoped cold review precedes one commit and close.

Exact paired activation and ordered-control evidence is deliberately not part of this ticket; it lands at the supported-alternative boundary in fz-kdt.64.

comments.text: DUPLICATE FOLDED (2026-09-03): fz-kdt.182 filed the same defect from the fz-kdt.120 research -- Types::union(empty_list(), list(int)) interns as `[] | [int]` though is_subtype(empty, list_int) holds (identical=false, is_equivalent=true, mutual subtypes), and fz-kdt.120's rule makes it visible (reduce at a ground reducer answers Known { result: [] | [int] }). Measured downstream at 0889c0b3a: activation keys carrying a `[] | [T]` union across the corpus: 1 at base (main/0#lambda@476-519/2[{any, any}, [] | [{any, any}]]), 0 under 120's prototype; render-identical duplicate executable keys 67 -> 40. So 120 does not need this first, but this ticket's "mutually-subtype types intern to one ID" is the general cure. 182 closed.

Third cold review of .48.4 (3cf777603, 2026-09-16), findings outside .48.4's scope, recorded for planning: (1) json_roundtrip carries 2 canon FALSE DIFFERENCES today: Ty(174) '{:error, binary} & not({any, any, any})' is mutually subtype with Ty(78) '{:error, binary}' (and the same pair under a ':nil |' union). A negative factor of DISJOINT ARITY (a 3-tuple carved out of a 2-tuple clause) is vacuous and nothing prunes it at intern; the absorber cannot see it (one clause, no siblings). Factor-level pruning, not axis-level; not covered by any open .48 sub-ticket; json_roundtrip is not in the census TARGETS so the ratchet does not catch it. Over a 10-fixture sweep it is the only fixture with false differences (2), 53 canon duplicates total. (2) Of the ~5% of intern calls that miss the index-first lookup, most still normalize onto an id the index already holds: 7,198 lookup misses vs 1,036 arena inserts on enum_take_drop_split (~6,100 full normalizations per compile for nothing). Next available reuse after the lookup.

Cold review of .48.6 (2f4e77719, 2026-09-16), residues measured, not filed: (1) canon is not injective-up-to-equivalence on the list axis for a multi-clause axis whose clauses cover one single-clause axis, e.g. list(int) | (list(int|:a) \ non_empty_list(int)) is equivalent to list(int|:a) but interns and renders apart; absorb_axis cannot see it (the wider clause is not contained in the union of the narrower ones' spellings). Randomized model sweep: 28 (flat) / 142 (nested) such ordered pairs at 2f4e77719, down from 1136 / 1232 at its parent, so .48.6 shrinks the class ~97% / ~88% and does not create it. (2) var-bearing list clauses that need element arithmetic are left as built at the boundary (variable-aware meet is out of scope), so non_empty_list(a) and non_empty_list(a) \ non_empty_list(int) are two ids that canon renders the same: counted by the census as one denotation, two ids. (3) instantiate's var-as-atom property: 10 of 600 random var-bearing list expressions reach a different id substituting first vs normalizing first, none equivalent, identical set on parent and .48.6.

title: Intern one Ty per denotation at the sole type boundary
